newsitem.title: UK: Northern Electric rejects CE Electric bid.
newsitem.headline: Northern Electric rejects CE Electric bid.

text.p: British regional electricity company (Rec) Northern Electric on Monday rejected a hostile takeover bid from CE Electric at 630 pence per ordinary share with a total value of $1.225 billion.

It said it had talks which culminated on Sunday in a proposal from CE Electric, which is 70 percent owned by CalEnergy, that it should enter into negotiations about an offer at around 700 pence per share.
Northern Electric said in a statement its board was scheduled to consider the situation this morning, but "instead the bidder chose to launch a hostile offer at a reduced price."
It said it would bring forward publication of interim results to demonstrate its "strong trading performance and cash flow."
Northern Electric shares, which had struggled to show any substantial premium to the 6.30 pounds ($10.06) bid price earlier, climbed to 650 pence, up 130 pence, by 1435 GMT.

CalEnergy chairman and chief executive David Sokol had said he felt the offer was "a very full price," and hoped for a recommended bid for Northern Electric, which is facing its second bid since it successfully fought off Trafalgar House, now owned by Kvaerner, last year. ($1=.6264 Pound)
